sentence: This project studies how a molecule in liver lymphatic endothelial cells regulates immune responses and bile duct injury in a rare liver disease.
This project applies molecular technology and computational biology to understand the health-disease continuum, including genetic susceptibility and molecular mechanisms of disease onset.
This project builds a wireless coil array and a cloud-based data processing workflow to make wireless MRI possible.
This project gives bioinformatics support to all projects and combines analysis with wet-lab sequence generation in one unit.
This project re-engineers a mouse line that carries a green fluorescent protein indicator so that it makes red fluorescent protein indicators instead.
This project coordinates a center that makes animal models of rare and undiagnosed diseases for patients and for studies of personalized medicine.
This project studies how live engineered bacteria can deliver a peptide drug by mouth to treat autoimmune disease.
This project uses bioinformatics and computational biology to understand changes in chromatin structure and transcription elongation in cancer.
This project tries to silence HIV in infected cells by delivering CRISPR-based gene therapy that is expressed only in those cells.
This project studies how chemical exposures and metabolic responses during pregnancy affect the risk of breast cancer before menopause, using prenatal serum.
This project supports research on the brain circuits behind addiction by monitoring neural activity and neurotransmitter release and by manipulating those circuits.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms behind sweat gland development and how progenitor cells respond to environmental cues.
This project builds a spatial omics platform to find out how a schizophrenia risk gene regulates RNA splicing and localization in neurons.
This project collects and stores biospecimens and develops and validates molecular tests based on biomarkers for breast cancer.
This project studies how an immune checkpoint pathway helps cancer resist immunotherapy and how it relates to immunosuppression caused by cannabis use.
This project studies patterns and causes of cancer, looks for biomarkers, and tests ways to prevent and control cancer.
This project uses human neurogenesis to find out what regulatory proteins mutated in autism spectrum disorders do at the molecular level.
This project builds a platform that tests many variants at once and uses a machine learning model to predict the effects of more variants.
This project studies how the many nuclei inside skeletal muscle fibers keep muscle size and function and how this goes wrong during aging.
This project studies how a phosphatase drives invasion of glioblastoma brain cancer cells and tries to develop strategies to target it.
